title: The Vamana Purana — chapters 1–69
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa; the Vāmanapurāṇa as it survives is a Shaiva text of north India, and GRETIL's e-text follows A. S. Gupta's edition (Varanasi 1967), which carries chapters 1–69 of the Purana.
description: The Vāmana Purāṇa tells the deeds of Vishnu's dwarf incarnation and, around them, the pilgrimage geography of north India and the worship of Shiva: the birth of the dwarf and the sacrifice of Bali that he brought to an end, the great pilgrimage places on the Sarasvati and in the Himalaya, the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice, and the vows, gifts and purifications the reader is to observe. Its chapters on the tīrthas are among the fullest of any Purana.
historicalContext: The Purana is a witness to the meeting of Vaishnava narrative and Shaiva worship in the medieval north, and it preserves in its pilgrimage chapters a description of the sacred landscape before the modern sites were settled.
availabilityNote: Partial: chapters 1–69 of the Purana in the edition GRETIL publishes, 4,516 verses, streamed from GRETIL at read time. The edition's text stops at chapter 69 and the remaining chapters are not published in this transcription; the work is not claimed as complete, and the availability note is part of the record rather than a defect of the import.
